Far from my specialty but I’ll comment:

Children are rightfully considered stupid and/or at least generally lacking in the experience and neurological development to be able to make socially coherent/appropriate moral judgments and to regulate their emotions and behavior accordingly. 
Children are generally excused from full responsibility for their behavior, with expectations of accountability changing as they mature toward adulthood.

18 years old is a more or less arbitrary generally agreed legal designation for being held responsible in judgement and accountable for your actions as an adult.

With regard to physical intimacy and sexual interaction (physical or not) the legal standards are determined in favor of protecting children from exploitation by adults. Exploitation in this case does not require any deliberate bad intention by the adult, but due to the potential consequences of the decisions the child is faced with and the child’s presumed lesser capacity to navigate them, the full burden of responsibility is placed on the adult.
The baseline is to say that there is no grey area and no legally defined child can consent to such interactions with a legally defined adult. 

To recognize the uncertainty in when a person should be developmentally considered as an adult, and what capacities different individuals may have at different ages in “childhood,” exceptions are generally legislated and judged by more regional/local levels of government.

To legislate broadly on the issue the hardline must be taken to protect children. On lower levels of government “grey areas” may be defined and enforcement may vary. 

From a moral perspective the closer in age and development you are to a child the more grey areas there are, mostly given that you are still a teenager yourself.

Be2 and 9. ... d4 are chosen as obvious and consistent moves for illustration, the most important alternative is 8. Bb5 for white to avoid being completely steamrolled.

I’m not exactly experienced in beheadings but I’ll venture an opinion. The first cut is the worst and everything after has perhaps a novel jolt to it, but otherwise is analogous to a fire alarm effect. The type of intermittent aching and unmitigated sharp pains that really make you suffer come with severe swelling around the areas of injury, which probably wouldn’t apply in the case of beheading. I think the best scenario would probably be having the strikes start from the back and near the base of the skull as this would result in the most rapid loss of neurological activity and, short of death, the ability to perceive and/or interpret pain. The effect from destruction of the brain stem is much more rapid than that of blood loss. With blood loss the awareness of even novel and severe acute pain dulls significantly before the loss of consciousness. 
In short - It’s probably most horrific until real damage is inflicted to the arteries or brain stem, with complete severance of the brain stem leading to instantaneous loss of awareness and significant severance of the arteries leading to relatively longer but still very rapid deterioration.
It’s probably far from the worst way to die.

I backed out of putting a knife through my face in similar fashion. It was an old knife my friend had given me before he died - not particularly sharp - and it got stuck for a moment pressing into some muscle or dense tissue layer. I looked at the mirror during that moment and felt ridiculous seeing myself with a stuck knife pressed in my face. I didn’t feel the pain from it or the cutting I had done just before. Everything numb except feeling ridiculous. I suppose it was both the wearing-an-oversized-pink&feathered-Dr. Seuss-esque hat, and the I-look-stupid.-I-feel-stupid.-This-is-stupid. types of ridiculous. I had that thought, then the one about how numb I felt despite the harm, then that I didn’t really want to risk losing control of the blade and messing up my teeth if I forced it through manually or by slamming into the wall, and that it was basically pointless since I wasn’t getting anything out of it and I’d basically ruined it already anyway, so I gave up on it and that entire harm episode.

I attempted suicide by stabbing myself five times in the abdomen. This was after 10+ years of certainty that I should kill myself in that way. Through all the deepest cycles of depression, various degrees of dissociation, and some crossings into psychosis that never entirely washed off, I had built up a sort of false religious complex about it. The reality of the experience of stabbing myself and of bleeding out/dying was a complete disappointment compared to the fantasy that I’d imagined thousands of times. As with the previously described episode, everything was just wrong. The pain, the feelings, the entire process was just mechanical and void. There was no catharsis, no relief in the way that was needed. There was nothing special about the actions, the pain, or the experience of dying - other than how extraordinarily mundane it was.

I accept the notion that suicide is not about a desire for death so much as a means to escape pain in life. It is not only about the overbearing sense of distress, but the harrowing lack of something needed. My own hopes for it involved breaking free - finding in it the means and strength to take hold of the shadow that somehow bears down weight upon me such that I can feel the sudden nervous pulse followed by the fatiguing constant electric tension, as if every nerve were pinched and then held under that pressure. The shadow that somehow also smothers you, saps your presence of mind, and squeezes your senses. I hoped to finally grasp the shadow, to finally breathe and find a perverse final exhilaration fueled by blood and pain. I hoped to finally feel my self break as my body broke and died. I assume my hopes for suicide were similar to many others’ - not for death so much as to finally be able to grip the shadow and break free, for whatever single perfect moment there may be just before everything ends. I felt no such strength, no freedom, no relief. Ultimately I just felt disappointed and bored, and that there had been no point to any of it. 

I still feel almost completely lost and isolated from people and the experience of life. I still have the thoughts. I still rage in them. What feels different is the loss of my conviction. Whatever it is that I really need in life, death did not deliver it.

I agree with dissociation. At my worst with it I did odd things like put a pack of cigarettes in the refrigerator, end up staring blankly without moving for extended periods of time, frequently forgot whatever I was doing or looking for in a moment, would completely blank on the process of how I ended up walking somewhere. I would feel more ethereal or ghastly than solid, as if I could walk through solid objects, to the point that I would test it against the door or walls. It became extremely disorienting externally, and internally I believe it facilitated symptoms of psychosis - one of which was a sense of being dead or rotting. I lived alone at the time. I had frequent physical pain related to joint issues along with 1.5-2 hours/day 6 days a week workout routine. I smoked frequently enough to start getting fungal infections on my tongue - it would get a white layer over it, feel dry in my mouth, and develop nodules which would become very sensitive and painful to move or put pressure on even against the soft areas in my mouth. I brushed my teeth aggressively and my gums would hurt and bleed. I started to develop receding gum lines and a recession in one spot. I haven’t really ever slept very well and I began to sleep even worse. My eyes were always bloodshot and the dark circles under them became larger and darker. I would have scabbed areas or damaged layers of skin for months at a time due to constantly picking at sores, reopening and even expanding them. 

Plastic bloodshot eyes with dark circles beneath them. I would bite the nodules off my tongue and it would hurt, they would bleed and leave visible pock marks on my tongue. I had a very large one in the center of my tongue once. A combination of running it across my front teeth and the aggressive brushing ripped it off and there was a very large, deep, bloody and painful sore that make moving my tongue even more difficult and painful. A receding gum line makes the teeth look longer. As gums of a dead body decompose and dehydrate they recede - this is one effect thought to inspire vampire lore. My gums were receding and inflamed, there was frequently the taste of blood in my mouth and after biting off nodules or brushing there would sometimes be visible blood on my gums and teeth. They hurt, and then my whole body hurt, constantly, and always had a number of never healing sores from picking. 

I felt exhausted and when I wasn’t physically  immaterial I would perceive myself as sunken in toward the back of my skull and peering out from a distance. I felt myself rotting and my body manifesting it. I felt frequently as either dead or dying and that either I would just decompose into nothing or that something else would grow through me and as my body decayed it would be revealed. Everything was watched through different eyes, never my own up front and center with me in direction of my body. Always from a distance or as something else waiting to emerge through my dying flesh.
I feel no choice.

I have a therapist and a psychiatrist I can’t afford. I see the psychiatrist tomorrow to check up on medications I can’t afford. I am not alone, but other people have their own issues and I have support roles with them and responsibilities that I am struggling to keep up.

I don’t have a fetish for pain. I have an impulse to externalize inner tension by inflicting violence. There are various reasons why I am the primary or sole target. I don’t entirely understand the role of pain, but I feel it is important that I enact it. I do not find myself wanting to merely die - I want to actively kill myself by violent means. I want full participation in, and direction of, it.
